items.title: SP-API Release Notes
items.excerpt: Selling Partner API new features, software updates, and changelog.
items.body: For releases prior to January 19, 2022, refer to Announcements in the Selling Partner API GitHub repo . September 30, 2026 API changes Finance Remittance API v2026-03-17 Launched the Finance Remittance API, which you can use to programmatically retrieve vendor payment remittance data. The API provides payment and deduction details, associated invoices, dates, and identifiers, including invoice payments, deductions, vendor returns, and advertising transactions. You can use this API to access the same remittance data that is available in Vendor Central without manually exporting reports. Support API v2025-02-01 Launched the Support API. You can use this API to programmatically retrieve information about a selling partner's Amazon support cases, allowing you to monitor issues within your application and implement fixes from Selling Partner Support more quickly. A+ Content API v2020-11-01 Added support for the 19 Premium A+ content modules and five Brand Story content modules through the same operations used for Standard A+ Content. Added the createMedia , getMedia , and updateMedia operations. You can use these operations to create image and video media assets, retrieve media metadata and related pairings, and update media titles and accessibility descriptions used by Premium video modules. Data Kiosk API v2023-11-15 Added the Seller Analytics dataset . Use the Seller Analytics dataset to access information including sales, traffic, promotions, account health, search, reviews, defects, and returns. Updated the Analytics Economics dataset with deal, coupon, removal, disposal, and fuel fees. Delivery By Amazon API v2022-07-01 Added the invoiceId query parameter to the getInvoiceStatus operation. You can use this parameter to retrieve an invoice. Feeds API v2021-06-30 Added...

Recorded in Shenzhen, China, Bradley Sutton sits down with experienced Amazon seller and new Helium 10 team member Shawn Su to explore the advantages, tactics, and challenges shaping one of the world’s most competitive e-commerce communities. Shawn shares his journey from two unsuccessful product launches to building two six-figure Amazon brands. He explains how he discovers overlooked opportunities using narrow price filters, minimum search-volume requirements, weak competitor images, and low title density. He also reveals why the ability to test small orders, respond to reviews, modify products, and launch improved versions quickly may be a greater advantage than lower manufacturing costs. The conversation also examines a controversial tactic involving manufactured keyword demand. Some sellers use external traffic to make previously unknown search terms appear popular before launching new FBA listings. Bradley explains why a sudden search-volume spike does not always represent organic demand—and why sellers should investigate where that traffic is coming from before entering the market. items.title: #766 - From Royalty Checks to Amazon Millions
items.excerpt: A handmade Christmas gift became a patented product and a multimillion-dollar Amazon business. Discover the licensing, team-building, and growth strategies behind its success.
items.body: A handmade Christmas gift became a patented product and a multimillion-dollar Amazon business. Discover the licensing, team-building, and growth strategies behind its success. ► Watch The Podcasts On Youtube: https://www.youtube.com/@Helium10SeriousSellersPodcast?sub_confirmation=1 ► Instagram: instagram.com/serioussellerspodcast ► Free Amazon Seller Chrome Extension: https://h10.me/extension ► Sign Up For Helium 10: https://h10.me/signup (Use SSP10 To Save 10% For Life) ► Learn How To Sell on Amazon: https://h10.me/ft What began as a handmade Christmas gift eventually became a patented product, a successful licensing deal, and a multimillion-dollar Amazon brand. Super Blanky founder and CEO Karen Bonnici joins Bradley alongside her nephew and newest intern, Jack Lustig, to share the story behind the wearable blanket. After watching the children play with her original cape-style design, Karen developed its signature pocket sleeves, hand-sewed the first 500 units, and validated the idea through craft shows. Karen later licensed her patents and trademarks to a manufacturer that brought the product into Target with characters such as Jurassic Park and Paw Patrol. Although the arrangement generated approximately $4 million in first-year retail sales, Karen earned only a royalty percentage and had limited control over the brand’s direction. When the licensing business began to decline, she learned e-commerce, sourced her own inventory, and launched Super Blanky on Amazon with two SKUs. The brand generated approximately $75,000 in its first five months, reached $2.2 million in sales last year, and is now projected to more than double that revenue.
